summary: Google DeepMind launches an 'agentic video understanding' feature for Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, and 3.5 Flash-Lite that dynamically scans video segments instead of fixed-frame-rate processing, cutting token consumption by up to 88% and cost by up to 66% while improving accuracy by up to 7%.

mechanisms.reason: A stated technique (dynamic, goal-directed video scanning instead of fixed-FPS ingestion) is described with concrete figures showing reduced tokens and compute per video analysis task.
mechanisms.quote: reduce analysis costs by up to 66% and token consumption by up to 88%, while improving accuracy by up to 7%

mechanisms.reason: The efficiency-driven feature is being rolled out to consumer-scale surfaces, which would increase aggregate call volume even as per-call cost falls.
mechanisms.quote: We are also bringing the efficiency and quality improvements of agentic video understanding to billions of users across Google products.

practices.reason: Existing production models gain a stated, quantified improvement in cost, video understanding, and long-form video handling that a team could act on immediately via API config.
practices.quote: reduce analysis costs by up to 66% and token consumption by up to 88%, while improving accuracy by up to 7%

practices.reason: Dynamic FPS/tool-based video scanning is a reproducible technique on our own stack, enabled by a single API config flag, that cuts token and cost overhead for video workloads.
practices.quote: Instead of static processing where the model ingests media streams at a fixed frame rate, agentic video understanding enables Gemini to take an active, goal-directed role in determining what to watch, at what speed, and through which modality

practices.reason: Enabling the feature requires a documented API configuration change that engineering teams would need to test and roll into their video pipelines.
practices.quote: To enable it, simply set processing to "agentic" in the API configuration.
